scope: Proposition 5.5 of the manuscript “Renewal and changes of law for critical honeycomb walks” (preprints/Renewal-and-changes-of-law-for-critical-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d179fa55e4b82fed), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every nonnegative function f of an irreducible, with p(f) < ∞, and every ϵ > 0, ∑︂ R≤h≤2R Dh ⎡ ⎣ ∑︂ i in the first path f(Ii) ⎤ ⎦ ≤ CϵR−5/4+ϵ p(f). (15) Either path can carry the mark. If the two bottom ports instead have any prescribed separation, while the top ports remain adjacent, the right side becomes CϵR−1/2+ϵp(f). In that second estimate, requiring the marked path to contain at most R3/4−δ increments improves the bound by R−δ+ϵ, with the exponent slacks combined in the constant.
